title: implement ResidualBlock

atoms.evidence: self.left = Sequential(Conv2d, BatchNorm2d, ReLU, Conv2d, BatchNorm2d); self.right = nn.Identity() or Sequential(Conv2d, BatchNorm2d); self.relu = ReLU()
forward: x_left = self.left(x); x_right = self.right(x); return self.relu(x_left + x_right) — the defining ResNet pattern
right branch when shapes mismatch: Conv2d(in_feats, out_feats, kernel_size=1, stride=first_stride) — 1x1 conv used purely to match channel count + downsample, no spatial mixing
first_stride > 1 on the left's first Conv2d AND on the right branch's 1x1 conv; the exercise explicitly hinges on whether is_shape_preserving = (first_stride==1 and in_feats==out_feats)
ReLU() used inside the Sequential and after the add, composed not implemented

atoms_in_seed_but_not_actually_present.reason: seed predicted this for exercise 7 but the skip-add is a pure same-shape elementwise add (left/right branches are shape-matched by construction); no broadcasting fires

notes: Densest architecture exercise so far: 6 atoms. First exercise where residual-skip-add, 1x1-conv-channel-reshape, and conv-stride-downsample all co-fire — these three form a tight ResNet 'downsampling block' cluster. The shape-preserving vs downsampling branching is the genuine pedagogical content.
